unresolved.note: Register records all34distinct input works across40references. Primary study content was not inferred from book-review titles or inaccessible article metadata; those entries remain context or unresolved.

White2021critique added as challenges to AAR caribou interpretation. Lemke2021reply identified but not read; its arguments are not guessed. New target-species and chronometric evidence could change assessment.

Author full text confirms calibrated archaeological chronology, unlike abstract-only BP wording. Phase bounds are approximate regional syntheses and do not date all communities or substitute for source-level age models.

The exact2022Wisconsin Northwoods title occurs in Iowa State commencement underGraceHartman, whereas inputattributesG.H.Tomasi. Full repository record/text needed before attaching Ojibwe-specific historical claims.

corrections.note: 14,000–13,000calBP descriptions date landscape/channel development. Talbot2021expects~13ka fromClovis technology; Nash2024reports direct dating still pending. Neither establishes direct14ka human arrival.

3000–300BP is not50–1500CE. If calibrated and1950-based it converts to astronomical-1050 through1650(1051BCE–1650CE). Since the cited abstract's calendar convention is unverified, no corrected mappedspan is inserted. Likewise2200–1500BP wouldnot50–500CE;1500–450BP wouldnotexact500–1500CE.
10,800–10,00014CBP and12,200–11,600calBP are not interchangeable full-event brackets. Lothrop2016gives theYD broadly12,900–11,600calBP;12,200–11,600calBP is itsMiddlePaleoindian analytical phase.
Primary Bayport outcrops are~170km fromHipwater. Nearby secondary glacial deposits remain possible. Describing this as demonstrated local procurement or a fixed short annual range is unsupported.

Lemke2015's27Michigan specimens include1archaeological and26paleontological remains. Abundance/ecological presence is not27hunted animals or proof of a caribou-exclusive economy; submerged cervidtooth is not securely species-specific here.

FittingandCleland1969place agriculture-favorable Carolinian province in southern UpperGreatLakes, not northernCanadianprovince. They explicitly project adaptations,not ethnic groups; artifactratios are not direct demographiccounts.

Peterson2024is a bookreview. PrimaryKooiman/Walder2019revises apparentAD1630pottery/tradeassociation: pottery-making endsby1500, beads manufacturedafter1650. This does not support uninterrupted50–1500occupation or allIndigenouspeople leaving1500.
SleepingBearPointabstract's past2000years refers to environmentalframework, not a directly boundedoccupation. Dune/reworkingevidence cannot alone establish periodicvillage rebuilding.

FultonandYansaprimarypublishertextstates2021onlinepublication;NelsonandMacdonaldlisted2019ratherthaninput2021. Kolb1997is a bookreview of1996editedvolume. Michalak2017isBooksandArts commentary. Allgaier/Codding2023isGreatBasin,andAnderson2025Southeast; neither supplies directGreatLakes evidence.

No source-supported resident-count series was recovered. Date/sitefrequency, toolstone distances and artifact numbers are not population estimates. Earlypresence does not prove uninterrupted local communities or a fixed descendant genetic line.
